messages.author: 021684469a76af99
messages.subject: Stochastic mapping (stratified): "Error in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root"
parts:
Hi Nick
when trying to run your stochastic mapping script for a stratified analysis under DEC, I get the following error:

Failure on stochastic mapping attempt #1/100 tries. Holding at success #0/50.
[1] "Error in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root_branch_of_subtree : \n  non-conformable arguments\n"
attr(,"class")
[1] "try-error"
attr(,"condition")
<simpleError in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root_branch_of_subtree: non-conformable arguments>

The same script works for DIVALIKE, though. 

I am using an "area_allowed" matrix and I assume that this may be the reason, because when I run the script without enforcing the areas allowed matrix then the BSM works. 
However, the outcome has non-adjacent areas as an ancestral state, which I consider implausible. Hence my attempt to rule them out by using an 'areas_allowed' file. 

I am attaching all files plus the script I am using. 

Best
Frank

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Stochastic mapping (stratified): "Error in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root"
parts:
Hi -- this is probably something about the areas_allowed matrix reducing the state space to a single area in a certain time bin, thus creating something that R misinterprets as a vector rather than a matrix, or something like that -- a danger of R's "trying to guess what the user wanted" system.

I thought I had all of these fixed, but perhaps not -- I will take a look when I get a chance. 

Cheers!
Nick

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Stochastic mapping (stratified): "Error in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root"
parts:
Hi Frank et al.,

1. I believe I've fixed this error with area_allowed in BSM one -- the error involved the case where the areas_allowed matrices through time created states_lists for each time bin, but when all of the states_lists for all time-bins were put together, the full list still did not equal the full list of states calculated based on the input areas list and the maxareas argument. (E.g., in these inputs, all of the areas_allowed matrices were the same.)

In general, as I have mentioned before, areas_allowed and areas_adjacency matrices are a crude way to control how the states_list changes by time-period, really it's only appropriate for simple situations like island-disappearance-back-in-time, like Hawaii:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#areas_allowed_matrix2
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#better_than_adjacency

 For more complex situations, manually specify your states_lists by time-bin:

Manual modification of states_list (list of geographic ranges, a.k.a. the list of states in the state space)
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#manual_modify_states

Re-using the manually modified of states_list
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#reuse_modified_states

Manually modify the states list in time-stratified analyses
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#modified_states_stratified



2. I also added an error check for BSM if the input areanames are not single-letter codes.

3. Re-install from GitHub to get the fixes.

4. Frank's files attached with minor changes, "NJM" for the ones that aren't e.g. working directory etc.

Cheers!
Nick

On Sunday, March 24, 2019 at 9:04:55 PM UTC-3 nickmat...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Frank et al.,

1. I believe I've fixed this error with area_allowed in BSM one -- the error involved the case where the areas_allowed matrices through time created states_lists for each time bin, but when all of the states_lists for all time-bins were put together, the full list still did not equal the full list of states calculated based on the input areas list and the maxareas argument. (E.g., in these inputs, all of the areas_allowed matrices were the same.)

In general, as I have mentioned before, areas_allowed and areas_adjacency matrices are a crude way to control how the states_list changes by time-period, really it's only appropriate for simple situations like island-disappearance-back-in-time, like Hawaii:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#areas_allowed_matrix2
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#better_than_adjacency

 For more complex situations, manually specify your states_lists by time-bin:

Manual modification of states_list (list of geographic ranges, a.k.a. the list of states in the state space)
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#manual_modify_states

Re-using the manually modified of states_list
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#reuse_modified_states

Manually modify the states list in time-stratified analyses
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#modified_states_stratified



2. I also added an error check for BSM if the input areanames are not single-letter codes.

3. Re-install from GitHub to get the fixes.

4. Frank's files attached with minor changes, "NJM" for the ones that aren't e.g. working directory etc.

Cheers!
Nick

To: bioge...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Stochastic mapping (stratified): "Error in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root"

 

Hi -- this is probably something about the areas_allowed matrix reducing the state space to a single area in a certain time bin, thus creating something that R misinterprets as a vector rather than a matrix, or something like that -- a danger of R's "trying to guess what the user wanted" system.

 

I thought I had all of these fixed, but perhaps not -- I will take a look when I get a chance. 

 

Cheers!

Nick

when trying to run your stochastic mapping script for a stratified analysis under DEC, I get the following error:

 

Failure on stochastic mapping attempt #1/100 tries. Holding at success #0/50.

[1] "Error in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root_branch_of_subtree : \n  non-conformable arguments\n"

attr(,"class")

[1] "try-error"

attr(,"condition")

<simpleError in condprobs_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_root_branch_of_subtree: non-conformable arguments>

 

The same script works for DIVALIKE, though. 

 

I am using an "area_allowed" matrix and I assume that this may be the reason, because when I run the script without enforcing the areas allowed matrix then the BSM works.

Frank

On Tue, Jun 20, 2023 at 10:38 AM José Ribeiro <jozeca...@gmail.com> wrote:
Ok, NIck. Thank you anyway.
Is it weird if I run a stratified DIVALIKE + j model, to do stochastic mapping simulations and provide any discussion on that result, taking into account the ancestral ranges of my best model with a trait?

Hi -- it's not weird at all.  You can even stochastically map the geography & trait separately, and then summarize across both.  Whether or not this is useful depends on e.g. the certainty of the trait reconstruction.  If you have close to 100% confidence in the trait reconstruction at the nodes of interest, stochastic mapping the trait doesn't add much.

Cheers,
Nick
